question: Is the 658,333-doc medium bucket (601-6000 chars) genuinely complete, or truncated?
method: 1. Deterministic sample: every 500th medium doc = 1,316 docs
2. Cross-matched against ALL local artifacts (crawl checkpoints + vault staging): 100% traceable
3. Full sweep of all 1,087,324 master docs vs artifact lengths: 136,664 have longer artifact text
4. Sample verdict on those (200 docs, deterministic): 185/200 same ending (CLEANED, not truncated), 0 cut early, 10 tiny-delta Gutenberg edits, 5 unclassifiable
5. Cleaning explanation: master build runs merge->clean (boilerplate stripped), so master text is INTENTIONALLY shorter than raw artifacts

verdict.medium_bucket_genuinely_complete: 97.9% identical to source artifacts; no true truncation found beyond the known problem-doc set
verdict.the_136664_artifact_longer_docs: NOT defects — they are the cleaned master copies of raw artifacts (135,216 of 136,664 gain <1K chars; 185/200 sampled end at the same content)
verdict.true_truncation_targets: 214 verified recoveries (manifest v1) + 2,197 capped upstream (cannot recover locally)

honest_limits: the medium-bucket verdict is sample-based (1,316 of 658,333); the full sweep proves artifact-longer docs end at the same content as their artifacts, so the completeness claim is strong but not per-doc certified
the 5 unclassifiable cases are recorded, not smoothed over
